figure_inventory.description: A tessellation inside a thick red rounded rectangle (landscape, no labels), pieces outlined in black: regular HEXAGONS filled light orange (flat top and flat bottom) and equilateral TRIANGLES filled light blue, fitting with no gaps (2 hexagons and 2 triangles meet alternately at every vertex, triangles point up and down alternately in the gaps). The hexagons have horizontal top and bottom edges. By counting: 6 complete hexagons (two rows of 3; the second row is shifted half a hexagon pitch to the left of the first), 20 triangles (5 bands of 4, up-pointing, down-pointing, up, down, up, whole or nearly whole), plus half hexagons and partial triangles cut off by the red frame along the top, bottom, left and right edges (the top strip shows 4 half-hexagons alternating with 4 up-pointing triangles whose apexes touch the top edge; a thin strip at the bottom shows 4 cut-off triangles and slivers of the next hexagon row). Side of the hexagon = side of the triangle. [Checked against the page picture: confirmed; the diagram uses the clipped lattice geometry (6 whole hexagons, 15 whole triangles, 13 + 9 pieces cut by the frame).]

A blue dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) filled with an isometric (triangular) dot lattice: 16 rows of dots, rows alternately offset by half a spacing, 30 dots in the odd rows and 29 in the even rows (counted by pixel analysis), the first row 30. The start of the pattern sits at the top-left, drawn with thin red outlines: 3 regular hexagons filled PURPLE and 10 equilateral triangles filled YELLOW-ORANGE (pale orange). Every hexagon side and every triangle side is 2 dot spacings long. Layout (hexagon H1 left, H2 right, H3 below between them): H1 and H2 sit side by side at the top with one down-pointing triangle above and one up-pointing triangle below their shared vertex (so 2 hexagons and 2 triangles meet there alternately); H3 sits below and between them, its top edge being the base of that lower up-pointing triangle. The 10 yellow triangles, band by band from the top: band 1: 2 up-pointing triangles, one on top of H1 and one on top of H2; band 2: 3 down-pointing triangles (left of H1's top, between H1 and H2, right of H2's top); band 3: 2 up-pointing triangles (below-left of H1, and the one between H1, H2 and H3); band 4: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H1, left of H3); band 5: 1 up-pointing triangle (lower-left of H3); band 6: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H3). Every placed hexagon is therefore surrounded by alternating triangles and hexagons as in P04-pattern-1. Still empty: the down-pointing triangle slot at the right of the H2/H3 junction, and everything to the right of and below the cluster. The rest of the lattice is blank. [Checked against the page picture: confirmed (3 purple hexagons, 10 yellow triangles, hexagon side = triangle side = 2 dot spacings).]

A blue dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) containing square dot paper (45 dots across, 18 dots down; counted by pixel analysis). At the left, a pattern of 16 regular OCTAGONS filled pale green (4 octagons across x 4 octagons down, edge to edge; each octagon is 4 dot-spacings wide and 4 tall with its 4 corners cut off by 1 dot-spacing) and 9 SMALL SQUARES filled pale blue, drawn tilted by 45 degrees (diamond orientation; diagonal 2 dot-spacings) in the gaps between each group of 4 octagons: 3 squares in each of the 3 gaps between the octagon rows = 9 squares (counted). Thin cyan outlines. Dots inside the pattern are faintly visible. The pattern occupies dot columns 2-18 and dot rows 2-18 (from the left and top), the dot paper to its right is empty. Marked points: 4 RED dots on the 4 corners (top, left, right and bottom vertices) of the right-most of the 3 blue squares in the topmost row of squares; at each marked point 2 octagons and 1 square meet. Nothing else is marked. [Checked: confirmed; note the octagons are drawn on dot paper with straight sides 2 and slanting sides 1.414 dot spacings, so they are only close to regular.]

A red dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) with square dot paper (45 dots across, 16 dots down; counted by pixel analysis). At the top-left a small cluster of 3 SQUARES (filled lilac, tilted, not aligned to the grid) and 2 TRIANGLES (filled orange), thin blue outlines, 5 RED dots on vertices. In dot spacings d: each square has side sqrt(5) d (a step of 2 across and 1 down); each triangle is isosceles with base 2d and the other two sides sqrt(5) d, so the triangles are NOT equilateral (base slightly shorter than the other sides; base angles about 63 degrees, apex angle about 53 degrees). Name the red dots A (left end of T1's vertical side, upper), B (lower end of that side), C (T1's apex, to the right), D (top apex of T2), E (T2's lower-right vertex). T1 = triangle A-B-C: a vertical side AB of length 2d on the left and its apex C to the right. T2 = triangle C-D-E: horizontal base CE of length 2d at the bottom and its apex D above. Square S1 (top-left) has the side A-C in common with T1 and the side C-D in common with T2. Square S2 (right) has the side D-E in common with T2. Square S3 (below) has the side B-C in common with T1. So around point C the shapes are S1, T2, S3 and T1 in that order with a gap of about 63 degrees (the size of a triangle's base angle) between T2 and S3, still to be filled. The rest of the dot paper is empty. [Checked: confirmed. First use of this picture is the 'Are the triangles equilateral?' question; there it is drawn without the 5 marked points.]
Second use of P05-grid-2 (the 3 lilac squares and 2 orange triangles on dot paper, with its 5 red marked points) for the 'What shapes are coming together at the marked points?' question.

A tall rhombus (vertices at top, bottom, left, right) filled pale cyan with a bright cyan outline, divided into 4 congruent right triangles by its two diagonals, which are drawn as thin white double lines crossing at the centre (one vertical, longer, one horizontal, shorter; the long diagonal is about 1.6 times the short one). RIGHT: the same equilateral triangle (apex up) with a black dashed vertical fold line from above the apex through the apex to below the base (the line of symmetry), and a grey dashed curved arrow with an arrowhead drawn across the lower part of the triangle from the right bottom corner towards the left bottom corner, i.e. the right half is folded over onto the left half. The sloping sides are the original sides of the equilateral triangle. No labels.

A thin double line (the join of two triangles) runs vertically from the apex straight down to the bottom vertex.
